title: CLIP-Style Symmetric Contrastive Loss
prompt:
A multimodal retrieval model receives paired image and text embeddings: row `i` in each batch is a matching pair. Implement their CLIP-style symmetric contrastive loss in PyTorch.

`clip_contrastive_loss(image_embeddings, text_embeddings, temperature=0.07, normalize=True)` takes matching floating tensors `(B, D)` with positive dimensions and returns a scalar loss. Optionally L2-normalize each row, form all pairwise dot products divided by temperature, and average image-to-text and text-to-image cross-entropy. Diagonal entries are positives; other batch entries are negatives.

Preserve dtype, device, and autograd without mutating inputs. Reject rank/shape mismatches or non-positive/non-finite temperature; `assert` is sufficient. Explain the effects of symmetry, normalization, and temperature.
